summary.headline: VRL Logistics Q4 FY26 total income rose 6% YoY to INR859 crore, with tonnage back to 3% YoY growth and EBITDA margin at 21.4%.
summary.overview: Q4 FY26 total income was INR859 crore, up about 6% YoY and 3% QoQ, helped by better realisation, new clients and return of previously lost accounts. Realisation per ton was about INR8,147, up roughly 3% YoY, and daily tonnage crossed 11,500 tons. EBITDA margin was about 21.4%, down about 190 bps YoY from an exceptional Q4 FY25 (23%+) but up about 48 bps QoQ. FY26 total income was about INR3,245 crore, profit INR237 crore (up about 29%), and EBITDA margin 20.8%. Management guided to FY27 tonnage growth of 6-7% and kept an EBITDA margin of around 20%+ despite fuel cost pressure, which it plans to pass on via selective rate hikes and fuel surcharges.

financial_highlights.change: down ~190 bps YoY; up ~48 bps QoQ

financial_highlights.metric: Return on capital employed / return on equity (FY26)

financial_highlights.change: INR101 crore vehicles; INR165 crore land and buildings

segments.name: Tonnage / volume
segments.commentary: Tonnage decline was 13% in Q1 FY26 and about 7% for full FY26; Q4 returned to about 3% YoY growth. April 2026 YoY volume growth was about 8% per management.

segments.name: Customer mix (Q4 YoY)
segments.commentary: New customers contributed about 17% of quantity, lost customers reduced volume by about 14%, and existing customers grew about 1%.

segments.name: Commodity mix (FY26)
segments.commentary: Textiles and cloth about 17-18%, agri (equipment, fertiliser, pesticides) about 10-11%, others (industrial, pharma, books, auto) about 5-6% each. Management says petrochemical-linked goods such as plastics are seeing lower demand.

segments.name: Booking mix (FY26)
segments.commentary: TO PAY and PAID spot bookings about 80%, ACCOUNT customers about 15-16%, FTL about 6-7%.

segments.name: Door-to-door
segments.commentary: Share rose to about 38-40% of commodities from about 33-34% earlier; realisation is about INR1-1.5 per kg higher for door delivery.

guidance_outlook: FY27 tonnage growth guided at 6-7% for the full year, with at least about 2% sequential growth each quarter.
New branches expected to add about 2-3% to FY27 tonnage; about 100 net new branches planned in FY27 (100+ gross openings, fewer closures).
EBITDA margin to be maintained around 20%+ (near 21% in Q1 FY27 per management), with some basis-point impact from the withdrawal of bulk fuel purchase.
FY27 capex guided at INR300-350 crore: about INR100-150 crore for vehicles and INR200+ crore for land and buildings.
Depreciation not expected to rise materially because most new investment is in land (non-depreciable).
Fuel price pass-through via selective route rate hikes, chargeable-weight change (1 cubic feet from 8 kg to 9 kg on certain routes) and fuel surcharge in contracts.
capex_capacity: Fleet: about 6,000 owned vehicles per management; vehicle count fell from about 6,100+ to about 5,900 YoY, with about 500 additions planned in FY26 (100+ done, about 400 more by December 2026) and no scrappage planned.
Network: about 1,293 branches and 50 trans-shipment hubs across 24 states and 4 UTs as of March 2026; about 110 branches opened in FY26 with about 55-60 closed, net about 40-50.
Vehicle life: normal replacement at up to 15 years; earlier only for outdated or accident-damaged vehicles.
About 77% of fleet debt-free and 14% fully depreciated.
Hubs in pipeline: 2-3 locations including Nagpur and Raipur.
demand_pricing: Q4 volume growth came from new customers and return of lost accounts after contract restructuring; management says lost customers are returning due to service levels.

Fuel: diesel prices rose about INR3 recently; management said it has passed through on selected routes but not across the network, and that a 2x increase in rates within a week means pricing will be reviewed over 1-2 months.
Fuel procurement cost per litre rose from INR84.52 to INR85.54 as direct refinery purchase fell from 41% to 36% of volume (bulk purchase withdrawn).
Competition: most of the industry is unorganised; VRL says it is at a premium to unorganised operators but comparable to organised players and express cargo on corporate accounts.
Demand headwind: petrochemical and crude-linked goods such as plastics are seeing weaker demand, per management.

qa_highlights.question: What is the FY27 volume growth outlook and what efforts drive it?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects at least 6-7% full-year tonnage growth and about 2% sequential growth per quarter, driven by completed rate rationalisation, marketing, new branches and new customers.

qa_highlights.question: Will fuel-driven price hikes hurt volumes, and how is fuel cost passed on?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said volume pressure is from weak petrochemical-linked demand, not fuel prices. Hikes were applied on selected routes, with fuel surcharges in contracts; April 2026 YoY volume grew about 8%.

qa_highlights.question: What is the margin impact of lower bulk fuel purchase?
qa_highlights.answer: Some basis points of margin impact; management said it is flexible to hold EBITDA around 20% and the bulk purchase facility has already been lost.

qa_highlights.question: Why did lorry hire charges rise?
qa_highlights.answer: Fleet fell from about 6,100 to 5,900 vehicles while tonnage grew, so outside hired vehicles were used to carry the extra volume, plus higher lorry hire rates.

qa_highlights.question: What is the new branch contribution and depreciation outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: New branches contributed about 1-1.5% of Q4 growth; FY27 branches expected to add 2-3%. Depreciation is not expected to rise much, as land is a large share of new investment.

qa_highlights.question: What is the business mix and competitive positioning?
qa_highlights.answer: Mix is about 80% spot (TO PAY/PAID), 15-16% account, 6-7% FTL; door-to-door about 38-40%. Rates are at a premium to unorganised players and comparable to organised players.

risks_watch: Fuel price volatility and geopolitical risk; the pass-through lag could compress margins in the near term, per management's own caveat.
Weak demand in petrochemical-linked commodities (plastics etc.) could offset recovery.
Reliance on hired vehicles (lorry hire cost rose) while owned fleet shrinks.
Achievement of 6-7% FY27 volume growth depends on net new branches (about 100) ramping up.
Management did not disclose kilometre-based metrics; lead distance is about 270-280 km and capacity 15-18 tons.
summary.management_tone: Confident on volume recovery and pricing pass-through, but cautious on near-term margins, with management stating some temporary disconnect is possible. Answers on fuel pricing and competition were direct, while the company declined to disclose the bus-business question (not in business) and kilometre data.
key_quotes: And ultimately, the cost, whatever additional costs will come, that needs to be pass it on to the customers.
So, on a full year basis, we are expecting around INR300 crores to INR350 crores capital expenditure.
But definitely, on a full quarter basis, we are planning to maintain similar EBITDA numbers.

About 100 net new branches planned in FY27 (100+ gross openings, fewer closures); new branches expected to add about 2-3% to FY27 tonnage
2-3 trans-shipment hubs in pipeline including Nagpur and Raipur

growth.why: Management guides FY27 tonnage growth of 6-7% (at least ~2% sequential per quarter), backed by about 100 net new branches (+2-3% tonnage), new customers and returning lost accounts, plus selective rate hikes; fleet is shrinking, so the volume plan relies more on branches than on vehicles, and the EBITDA margin is guided at about 20%+.
